### What happened?

With recent changes from v2.10 onwards, the old home assistant actions no longer behave as they did before.

Specifically:
```
  - action: music_assistant.get_library
    data:
      config_entry_id: <working-config-entry-id>
      media_type: podcast
      search: '<desired-podcast-title>'
    response_variable: latest_podcast
  - action: music_assistant.play_media
    target:
      entity_id: '<working-media-player-entity-id>'
    data:
      media_id: '{{ latest_podcast[''items''][0][''uri''] }}'
```
used to queue podcasts from the latest to the oldest, and skip any portions that have already been heard.

The same actions now resume the most recently listened episode (from where it was left off) and queue the remaining episodes in order from oldest to latest.

To try to resolve, I set up a HA rest_command as documented here:  https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/4701

Configuring that rest_command:
- using "start_item": "newest" plays the oldest episode for the specified podcast with nothing else queued; and
- using "start_item" "[search-string]" plays from the episode correctly identified by the search, with later episodes queued in the order

## What happened?

Setting up Spotify with the Soloist backend always fails with:

> The Spotify Soloist app downloaded from Spotify could not be used. Try again later.

(`soloist_invalid_archive` / `InvalidArchiveError`)

The download itself is fine — the release archive is fetched successfully. It is the archive validation in
`music_assistant/providers/spotify_connect/soloist/runtime.py::_extract_binary_from_archive` that rejects it:

```python
if name.name != "soloist":
    raise InvalidArchiveError(f"unexpected file in soloist archive: {member.name}")
```

Every regular file in the tarball has to be named `soloist`, but the archives Spotify currently serves contain
three files. Checked today for all three architectures:

```
x86_64 → ['CHANGELOG.md', 'THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt', 'soloist']
arm64  → ['CHANGELOG.md', 'THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt', 'soloist']
arm32  → ['CHANGELOG.md', 'THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt', 'soloist']
```

`CHANGELOG.md` is the first member, so the install aborts immediately and Soloist can never be installed.

Running MA's own validator (from the installed 2.10.1 package) against the archive the CDN serves right now:

```
$ python3 -c "..."
MA version: 2.10.1
ar

posts.excerpt:
I really like the queue and the autoplay features, but I think they clash in practice:
If I'm playing a song with autoplay enabled, MA dynamically adds tracks to the queue.If I try to add a track to the queue manually using "Add to queue", it gets placed all the way at the end of that auto-generated list, meaning I won't hear it for a long time. You can do "Play next", but that will place it at the top of the queue and when I add multiple tracks to the queue they will be placed in reverse order (last in, first out).
Spotify solves this by having two seperate queues (even if they look like a continuous list visually). Queued items appear in the first queue and have a queue icon. Items that play automatically afterwards, like items from a playlist and autoplay tracks appear in the second queue. The first queue has priority, and when that one's empty, tracks from the second queue get played.
I like that view because then you can also turn autoplay off while playing music, and the first queue will still be played but no autoplay tracks will be played anymore.
posts.title: Self made queue and playlist/autoplay queue split

### Summary

`parse_title_and_version` (in `music_assistant/helpers/util.py`) can badly truncate a track's display title when the title legitimately contains " - " as part of the title itself, rather than as a separator before a version/remix suffix. The standard-parsing pass uses `re.findall(r" - .*", t)`, which greedily matches from the first " - " to the end of the string — so any title with more than one meaningful segment separated by " - " loses everything from the first occurrence onward.

### What happened?

A legacy AirPlay 1 / RAOP receiver — Marantz NR1506 (2016), `Server: AirTunes/190.9` —
can never be started. Music Assistant correctly selects RAOP, but `cliairplay` aborts
during the handshake after ~2 s and the player is dropped from its group.

The failing step is `auth-setup`. The receiver advertises `et=0,4` in its `_raop._tcp`
TXT record, so it claims FairPlay/MFi support; `stream.py` passes those properties
through as `--et 0,4`, cliairplay performs `POST /auth-setup`, and the receiver answers
`RTSP/1.0 500`. cliairplay treats that as fatal.

So this is not cliairplay doing something unrequested — the device asks for it and then
refuses. The problem is that a failed `auth-setup` ends the connection instead of
falling back to the plain RAOP handshake, which leaves the receiver permanently
unusable.

## Problem

The Home Assistant "homeii-music-flow" Lovelace card (and similar web dashboards)
can read artwork and drive Sendspin only through Music Assistant's Direct API
(direct WS/HTTP from the browser to the MA server). This requires the MA web server
to allow the dashboard's cross-origin requests.

When the card is used with the Music Assistant add-on (host_network, port 8095) served
at https://<host>:8095 while the dashboard is served at https://<host> (different origin),
the browser blocks every Direct API call: the MA web server sends no
Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so fetch() fails the CORS preflight.

Diagnostics from the card confirm: "Direct Music Assistant API is blocked by the
browser before HOMEii receives a response. This is usually CORS/preflight."

Verified directly: GET to https://<host>:8095/ with an Origin header returns no
Access-Control-Allow-Origin in the response, so the request is rejected.

## Expected behavior

Allow configuring a list of allowed CORS origins (like Home Assistant's
http.cors_allowed_origins), so web dashboards residing on a different origin can use
the Direct API. This also unlocks Sendspin, which requires Direct API access.

Casting to a sync group over Spotify Connect, the first press of the volume rocker jumps the whole group to ~96 and blasts every speaker.

`_sync_player_volume_to_spotify` in `providers/spotify_connect/provider.py` is meant to push the player's volume to the backend at session start, so the Spotify app's slider starts from the real level. It bails out first:

```python
player = self.mass.players.get_player(player_id)
if player is None or player.state.volume_level is None:
    return
```

A sync group never sets its own `volume_level`. It exposes `group_volume` (the max of its members) instead, which this doesn't read. So the push never happens, the backend stays at its 100 default, and the first press sends an absolute 96. `cmd_volume_set` on a group player redirects to `set_group_volume`, so that lands on every member at once.

First volume event of a session, with the members sitting at 29-44:

```
Received event [Spotify Connect/...]: volume {'max': 100, 'value': 96}
```

Add group-wide absolute volume and mute/unmute controls

Music Assistant currently provides individual volume/mute controls and a group volume control that preserves the relative volume differences between group members.

It would be useful to also have explicit group-wide controls:

1. Set all group members to the same absolute volume

Example: if speakers are currently at 12, 10, 7 and 15, setting “All” to 10 should result in 10, 10, 10 and 10.

2. Mute all / Unmute all

One action should mute every member of the current group, and another should unmute every member.

These controls should be available directly in the Music Assistant volume/group popup, so MA can be used as the central audio interface without needing to switch to Home Assistant, Sonos or another manufacturer app.

Ideally this should be generic for all supported grouped players, including Sonos, rather than being Sonos-specific.

After upgrading to 2.10.0 the Spotify provider no longer loads:

```

`migrate_provider_setup_data` moves each provider's setup-flow-owned keys from `values` into `setup_data`, but `PROVIDER_SETUP_FLOW_KEYS` deliberately skips `spotify`. So on an upgraded install the Spotify credentials stay in `values`.

This post is a concrete implementation proposal for how we can get hardware Squeezeboxes and software Squeezelite players, including piCorePlayer, to browse the library in Music Assistant.

## What is there now

Currently, MA supports playing music through Squeezelite players, and these players can control playback and skip to next track, and that's it. This support is mostly concentrated in [the `aioslimproto` package](https://github.com/music-assistant/aioslimproto).

For this proposal, we are only interested in the CLI, docs here: https://lyrion.org/reference/cli/introduction/

### Checklist

## What happened

A sync group that is **formed for an announcement but never reaches `PLAYING`** never schedules its idle-grace dissolve, so it stays formed indefinitely. While it lingers, an explicit `play_media` aimed at **one member** is redirected to the **group's** queue, so music intended for a single speaker plays on all 17 members of the group — and the member's `play_media_overrides_group: true` is never consulted.

This bit us in the real world: a per-room "welcome home" automation targeting exactly one speaker broadcast the whole house instead.

### The two halves

**1. The group never dissolves when the announcement fails.**

`providers/sync_group/player.py` (2.9.13, `_update_attributes`) only schedules the grace timer on a `PLAYING`/`PAUSED` → `IDLE` transition:

```python
if new_state == PlaybackState.IDLE and prev_state in (
    PlaybackState.PLAYING,
    PlaybackState.PAUSED,
):
    if self._attr_powered is not True:
        self._schedule_idle_grace_timer()
```

Forming a group for an announcement captures every member, but if the announcement audio never actually plays, the group goes `IDLE` → `IDLE`. `prev_state` is never `PLAYING`/`PAUSED`, so `_

### What happened?

Every track from the niconico (nicovideo) music provider fails with `track://<id> not found on provider nicovideo--xxxx`, and playback aborts with `no more tracks available`.

The track isn't the problem. niconico's watch API returns `null` for `viewer.existence.prefecture`, and the pinned `niconico.py-ma==2.1.0.post2` types that field as a non-optional `str`. Pydantic rejects the whole response, `get_watch_data()` returns `None`, and the provider reports the track as missing.

It is always **1 validation error** — `age` and `sex` validate fine, so `prefecture` is the only broken field.

1. Set up the niconico provider with a normal (non-premium) account.

 "existence": {"age": 26, "prefecture": null, "sex": "unanswered"}}

posts.excerpt:
### What happened?

When using the Web Player (Chrome/Edge/Firefox) as an active audio output, opening a second browser tab, duplicating the tab, or abruptly cutting off the audio stream leaves the previous HTTP streaming socket in a zombie state.

Instead of gracefully closing the existing session, Music Assistant continues pushing audio chunks to an unhandled/abandoned socket. This blocks the main Python Event Loop (aiohttp), causing rapid memory leaks and eventually leading to a system-wide crash via host OOM-Killer.

### What happened?

I have five Spotify Connect plugin instances set up, one per player, the way the plugin docs describe. After a server restart only one of them shows up as a device in the Spotify app. The other four get flagged "This provider requires attention" in Settings > Plugins.

The cause is a port collision. Each instance's go-librespot process starts at API port `127.0.0.1:38800` and only moves to the next port if 38800 is already taken. When all five start at once they all check 38800 before any of them has bound it, so one wins and the other four exit right away with:

- The server only logs `INFO ... Spotify Connect background daemon stopped for <name>` with no reason attached. You can't see the fatal error unless you set that plugin instance's log level to DEBUG.

posts.excerpt:
# Motivation

Music Assistant currently has excellent support for:

- Music Providers
- Player Providers

However, there is no generic concept for **Audio Input Providers**.

Many modern devices contain physical audio inputs:

- WiiM Amp / Amp Pro / Ultra
- HDMI ARC
- Analog Line In
- Optical In
- Bluetooth Input

These inputs are currently only usable inside the vendor ecosystem.

Example:

Turntable
    ↓
Phono preamp
    ↓
WiiM Amp Pro Line In

The WiiM digitizes the audio internally (48 kHz / 16 bit PCM) and can already distribute it to other WiiM devices.

What is missing is exposing this input as a Music Assistant Audio Source.

# Proposal

Introduce a new Provider type:

Audio Input Provider

which publishes one or more Sources:

- WiiM Line In
- WiiM HDMI ARC
- WiiM Optical In

These sources should behave like any other Music Assistant source and be routable to any player.

# Why this is useful

This would make it possible to:

- stream vinyl throughout the house
- distribute TV audio
- use physical inputs in automations
- route live audio to Sonos, Chromecast, Snapcast, etc.

instead of limiting them to a single vendor ecosystem.

# Notes

I investigated the WiiM HTTP API.

### What happened?

A track in my Apple Music library that is **greyed out (unplayable) in the Apple Music app itself** is reported by the Apple Music provider as `available: True`. MA queues it, attempts playback, and only finds out it is unplayable when Apple's `webPlayback` endpoint refuses it.

The cause is in `music_assistant/providers/apple_music/parsers.py`, `parse_track()` (~line 255):

```python
# Check availability: library tracks owned by user OR catalog items with playParams
is_library_track = is_library_id(track_id) and track_obj.get("type") == "library-songs"
has_play_params = attributes.get("playParams", {}).get("id") is not None
...
available=is_library_track or has_play_params,
```

For any `library-songs` object, `available` is `True` unconditionally — `playParams` is never consulted. Apple signals "this cannot be played" by omitting `playParams`, so the one signal that would identify an unplayable library track is discarded for exactly the objects where it matters.

`parse_album()` has the same shape a few lines earlier (`is_library_album or has_play_params`), so albums are likely affected the same way.

### Logs

Sanitized — provider instance IDs and library ide

posts.excerpt:
### Problem

When a player is part of a synced group, a pause command received from that player can pause the entire group. This can come from a physical play/pause button or the native device application.

For some players, that behavior is undesirable. A local or accidental pause on one portable speaker should not necessarily stop playback everywhere. I am seeing this with a Sonos Move used from Music Assistant alongside a Sonos Port / synced group.

This is especially relevant to the group-control routing introduced in [server PR #4950](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4950), which intentionally forwards physical controls from an AirPlay speaker to its active Sendspin group.

### Proposed behavior

Add a per-player setting for inbound transport commands while that player is synced or bridged into a group:

- **Propagate to group** — current behavior and default
- **Ignore** — discard play, pause, stop, previous, and next commands received from that player while grouped
- **Detach and apply locally** — remove that player from the group, then apply the command only to it

The setting should affect inbound transport commands only. Volume commands and normal group sync
posts.title: Per-player policy for transport commands from a synced group member

Music Assistant supports genres internally — `genres` controller, genre library items, and `get_genre_tracks()` in the queue builder — and `music_assistant.play_media` will happily play a `library://genre/<id>` URI. But neither HA service can *resolve* a genre by name, so scripts and voice assistants can't reach them.

**`handle_get_library`** (`homeassistant/components/music_assistant/services.py`): the schema accepts it via `vol.Required(ATTR_MEDIA_TYPE): vol.Coerce(MediaType)` — `GENRE` is a valid enum member — but the handler's dispatch has no `GENRE` branch and falls through to `raise ServiceValidationError(f"Unsupported media type {media_type}")`.

**`search_library`** (`controllers/music.py`): dispatches on ARTIST/ALBUM/TRACK/PLAYLIST/RADIO/AUDIOBOOK/PODCAST. No GENRE branch, though `MediaType.ALL` includes `GENRE` — which makes it look supported.

**Impact:** "play some jazz" can't be implemented. A script has no way to turn a genre name into a URI, so the workaround is a hand-maintained name→id map baked into the script — which silently plays the *wrong* genre if ids are ever renumbered.

### How is the MA server installed?

Docker container (`ghcr.io/music-assistant/server:2.9.10`), `network_mode: host`, on a Debian 13 LXC.

### The problem

`CacheController.set()` fails with `TypeError: default serializer exceeds recursion limit`. The exception is raised inside a fire-and-forget `asyncio.Task`, so it surfaces only as `Error doing task: Task exception was never retrieved` and the server carries on. posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.9.10 (also confirmed present in 2.9.9)

### What version of the Home Assistant Integration have you got installed?

Latest (HA 2026.7.4, MA HAOS add-on)

### The problem

**A user-supplied custom `music_app_token` (Apple developer token) is silently overwritten with the bundled shared token whenever the bundled token validates successfully.**

In `music_assistant/providers/apple_music/__init__.py`, `get_config_entries()` does:

```python
async with (
    mass.http_session.get(
        "https://api.music.apple.com/v1/test",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {MUSIC_APP_TOKEN}"},
        ...
    ) as response,
):
    if response.status == 200:
        values[CONF_MUSIC_APP_TOKEN] = f"{MUSIC_APP_TOKEN}"   # <-- unconditionally clobbers a stored custom token
        default_app_token_valid = True
```

Because the bundled token is almost always "valid" (it only tests for HTTP 200, not for rate-limit health), any custom developer token a user stores is reverted to the bundled one on the next config-entries load. The user has no indication this happened — the SECURE_STRING field is hidden when `default_app_token_valid` is true.
posts.title: Apple Music: custom music_app_token is silently overwritten by the bundled token whenever the bundled token validates (makes personal developer tokens unusable)

posts.excerpt:
### What happened?

I'm running multiple Spotify connect plugins to advertise different speaker groups as different "devices" within Spotify. This generally works well, however there is a start-up race condition.

Each plugin wishes to advertise itself, and will first check that it's preferred port (38800) is available. If it is found unavailable, then a different port will be chosen (usually incremented by 1). However, during a restart of music assistant, both plugins check port 38800 is free (which it is), and then try to startup using that port - at which point only one succeeds and the other enters an error state.

Manually reloading the plugin fixes the issue until the next restart, as during the reload, the second plugin correctly identifies that it's preferred port is taken and chooses a different port.

Music Assistant is slow to start some radios. Typically, https://stream.levillage.org/canalb takes ~9s to start on my setup. It seems that 5s come from this issue https://trac.ffmpeg.org/ticket/8104. `ffmpeg` takes time to properly identify the stream. Typically, `vlc` does not suffer of this issue. You can compare:

    ffmpeg -i https://stream.levillage.org/canalb -f alsa default

with:

    vlc https://stream.levillage.org/canalb

One workaround is to pass the the format and the codec to ffmpeg:

    ffmpeg -f mp3 -acodec mp3 -i https://stream.levillage.org/canalb -f alsa default    

MA could provide a way to associate format and codec to radio stream in the library. Even better, MA could semi-automatically fill these values.

### What happened?

Subscribing to WBUR's "The Midnight Rebellion" podcast RSS feed
(https://rss.wbur.org/the-midnight-rebellion/podcast) causes playback to
fail. The podcastfeed provider passes a cover-art JPG URL to ffmpeg as
if it were the audio stream, which of course fails to decode. (This is true of all WBUR's feeds, "Circle Round" is another example.)

**Root cause**

Each `<item>` in this feed contains *two* `<media:content>` elements —
one for the cover image, one for the audio — plus a standard
`<enclosure>` pointing at the audio, in this order:

```xml
<media:content url=".../Chap_4_1_1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" medium="image">

posts.excerpt:
### Problem

The Smart Playlist "Year" rule filters using the release year stored for the
album/track, which for compilations, "best of" albums, and reissues is the
reissue date — not the original recording/release year. This makes
decade-based smart playlists (e.g. "90s hits") unreliable for anything in
your library via a compilation.

Example: "Come Softly To Me" by The Fleetwoods, originally released in 1959
(Capitol Records), is in my library via the compilation "Come Softly To Me:
The Very Best Of The Fleetwoods" (1992, via Qobuz). A Smart Playlist rule
"Year: 1990-2000" picks it up, even though it's a 1959 track.

### Proposed solution

Add support for an "original release year" field (distinct from the
edition/compilation year) that the Smart Playlist Year filter can use when
available from the provider/metadata — similar to the year vs.
original_year distinction used by beets/MusicBrainz Picard.

### Alternatives considered

None that I know of within MA itself — happy to hear if there's already a
workaround.
posts.title: Smart Playlist "Year" filter: use original recording year, not reissue/compilation year

**Problem**

Music Assistant never expires player registrations. When a client device re-registers under a new id — app reinstall with an install-scoped id, factory reset, restored-from-backup, a client identity bug — the old entry stays in Settings → Players as "unavailable" forever. There is no TTL, no auto-hide, and no bulk cleanup: each orphan must be found and deleted one at a time.

We maintain Sendspin clients (an Android TV / Apple TV visualizer player, plus contributions to SendspinKit — e.g. Sendspin/SendspinKit#36), and a single client-side identity bug on one Apple TV produced **seven** orphaned "unavailable" copies of the same physical device on one server before anyone noticed. Cleaning that server took the player list from 66 to 48 entries, all removed one by one. We've since made our client ids reinstall-stable, but no client can prevent this class of cruft in general — factory resets alone guarantee a slow drip of orphans for every user, and every player provider (not just Sendspin) is affected.

**Proposal**

1. **Auto-hide unavailable players after N days** (configurable, e.g. default 30; off = current behavior). Hidden, not deleted — a hidden player that reconne

## Problem
There's currently no easy way to share what you're listening to with another MA user. Exporting a playlist as a file works, but it's not the same as a simple "hey, check out this track" moment — it requires extra steps and the recipient still has to manually import it.

## Proposed solution
A Share button in the player (and in context menus for tracks, artists and playlists) that generates a shareable link. When someone opens the link in their own MA instance, it resolves the item against their available providers automatically — regardless of which providers they use.

The key insight: user A on Spotify and user B on Apple Music can both open the same link and find the right track, because the link uses provider-agnostic identifiers (like ISRC or MusicBrainz ID) and falls back to a simple search if needed.

## Use cases
* Share a "now playing" status in chats or on social media
* Send a track or playlist recommendation to a friend who also uses MA

## Technical note
This would work similarly to the "My Home Assistant" button — a stateless redirect link where all the item info is encoded in the URL itself. No central database or storage needed.

I'd like to propose an API for pre-caching of music/podcasts for offline play. Current Sendspin requires a consistent and not too segmented internet connection between client and server, so it's hardly usable for spotty connections on roads and trains.

The idea is that offline-capable apps pre-cache these files to app-private storage, so it's explicitly _not_ meant to start a second music library for other apps or users to access. Rather, the cache would be used only by that app for offline play on planes, or to bridge timespans without internet, and for limited search to find such cached tracks. Apps would be aware of the canonical storage location on the server, so any metadata (playback history, listening position, favorites etc.) would still be persisted and visible to other clients, including pure Sendspin clients.

Clients of the proposed API would not necessarly get the original data. Rather, they receive a version targetted at their playback abilities, also taking into account reduced bandwidth. So the audio might be transcoded to a different codec, bit rate and/or bit depth. Volume-adjustments and other DSP workload might already be applied.

posts.excerpt:
Currently, as described in a comment [here](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966505097), Music Assistant disallows setting higher buffer sizes on machines at certain RAM thresholds.

This is an opinionated position, but disallowing a feature on an arbitrary threshold is removing some of the freedoms of the software user who may know the compromises made in order for it to work. Before this option was removed, I had run a perfectly stable server on a setting that is now no longer available to me (and the experience is now worse because of it).

I suggest that instead of removing the option from the frontend entirely, that the other buffer sizes are offered, and a user provided an appropriate warning that it may cause stability or OOM issues in some situations, if the hardware is below certain memory thresholds.

Additionally, I suspect that these thresholds have been set too high. I outline some thoughts about this [in this follow up comment](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966603603) on the same original issue.
posts.title: Allow higher buffer sizes on lower memory devices

Browsing the "Metal" genre shows a huge amount of music that isn't metal at all — mainstream rock, pop-rock, etc. mixed in with genuine metal albums. Traced the cause to `music_assistant/helpers/resources/genres/genre_mapping.json`: the top-level `metal` genre's `aliases` list includes `"Rock"`, `"Hard Rock"`, and `"Rock / Indie"` — all of which are also present in (or clearly belong to) the separate top-level `rock` genre.

Because `"Rock"` is a generic tag used across huge swaths of non-metal music (way more file libraries tag things simply `Rock` than tag them with an actual metal subgenre), this single alias entry ends up dumping a large share of a user's entire rock collection into the Metal genre. `"Hard Rock"` has the same problem to a lesser degree — it's a legitimate metal-adjacent term, but it's genuinely ambiguous/contested whether it belongs there, and it's also already a `rock` alias, so it's being double-counted.

posts.excerpt:
### What happened?

Starting the Deezer **Flow** (the default personalized flow) fails and nothing plays. Regular Deezer playback — recommended tracks, favorites, playlists, individual tracks/albums — works fine, so authentication / ARL is valid.

The server-side error is a Deezer GraphQL complexity rejection while fetching the flow batch:

```
GetFlowBatch: [GraphQLClientGraphQLError('The query exceeds the maximum complexity of 25000. Actual complexity is 45341')]
```

When triggered from Home Assistant via the `music_assistant.play_media` action, HA surfaces it as `500 - 500 Internal Server Error`. It also fails directly from the Music Assistant web UI when starting Flow.

It appears Deezer tightened the GraphQL "Pipe" API complexity limit (or the query grew), so the `get_flow_batch` query in [`music-assistant/deezer-python-gql`](https://github.com/music-assistant/deezer-python-gql) now exceeds the 25000 limit (~45000). Non-flow queries (recommended tracks etc.) stay under the limit and keep working.

### How to reproduce

1. Configure a working Deezer provider (valid ARL).

Summary

On a 4-core Intel N100 mini PC (Music Assistant 2.9, filesystem_local provider, 65,387 candidate tracks), the Sonic Analysis background scan projects 317–635 days to cover the full library (measured, not estimated — see below). Players exposed via the Plex Connect plugin never appear in Plexamp on iOS (even on same subnet, iOS Local Network permission ON, Private Wi-Fi Address OFF, and when they appear on desktop Plexamp).

Server side is healthy: the plugin starts cleanly, GDM advertising is active, and playback started from desktop Plexamp works perfectly.

Verified the fix: registering the player's identity on plex.tv via the official PIN flow (plex.tv/link) and publishing its local connection URI makes the player appear in iOS Plexamp, which then controls it through the plugin's existing local HTTP endpoints. > **Status: already fixed.** Resolved by music-assistant/server#4544 (merged 2026-07-02), which removes the legacy `/imageproxy?provider=&path=` query-string form and its `_is_safe_imageproxy_request_path` validator. Filed here for the public record per maintainer request to split the coordinated private report (`GHSA-5cv4-xxvj-mpvc`) into one item per finding. No further action needed beyond confirming the fix reaches a release.

## Summary — unauthenticated arbitrary image-file read via legacy `/imageproxy` (CWE-22 / CWE-23)

The deprecated `/imageproxy?provider=&path=&size=&fmt=` route was registered on the **unauthenticated** stream server. Its safety check accepted empty-scheme (local) paths and performed no absolute-path or containment validation, so a remote, unauthenticated attacker could read arbitrary image-extension files anywhere on the host filesystem — and extract embedded cover-art from arbitrary media files.

## Impact

```
GET http://<host>:<stream-port>/imageproxy?provider=builtin&path=/absolute/path/to/file.png
```

returned the file bytes with **no authentication**. Scope was constrained (not unrestricted `/etc/passwd` read), which is why it was rated HIGH rathe

Hi Team,

First of all, thank you for this amazing project! 

I would like to propose a clean, architectural solution for a persistent issue in the Media Browser (Browse view): the default sorting order.

## The Problem
Currently, when browsing local file-based systems (e.g., Local files, SMB shares), the default sort order is set to 'Original'. On Linux filesystems, 'Original' means the items are listed based on inodes/filesystem indexes, resulting in a completely scrambled, unreadable order. 

While users can manually switch the sort order to 'Alphabetical' on the UI, this setting is not persistent. Upon page refresh, pagination (loading more chunks), or navigating deeper into folders, the frontend reverts back to 'Original'. This makes browsing larger local directories highly frustrating.

### The Solution (Proposal)
Instead of trying to fix state persistence in the frontend or forcing a global default that might break streaming providers (like Spotify or Tidal, which rely on 'Original' to keep their curated order), **the default sort order should be handled at the Provider level.**

It would be amazing to have a dropdown setting within each Music Provider's configuration page:
posts.title: Provider-level default sort order for Media Browser

**Music Assistant version:** 2.9.3
**Provider:** Audiobookshelf (music provider)

### Symptom

The Audiobookshelf podcast sync (and the recommendations fetch) fail *wholesale* when a single podcast episode has an out-of-range year in its date:

```
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.tasks] Background task Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts failed: year must be in 1..9999, not 10909
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.music] Error while fetching recommendations from Audiobookshelf: year must be in 1..9999, not 40300
```

### Cause

An Audiobookshelf podcast had episodes whose date parsed to an out-of-range year (e.g. `10909`, `40300`). MA raises a `ValueError` building the `date`/`datetime`, and the exception propagates up and aborts the entire **Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts** background task (and the recommendations fetch). As a result **none** of the provider's podcasts/audiobooks import — not just the offending episode.

### Expected

An episode with an invalid / out-of-range date should still be **imported and shown — just with an empty / unset date** — and the sync should continue. A bad date value should degrade to "no date"; it should never skip the episode, and never abort th

While it's usually desirable for both speakers in a stereo pair to have the same volume level, sometimes there are a specific situations where it's desirable for one side to have more volume than the other.

For example:

- If one speaker has to be placed significantly further away from the listener, the soundstage won't be centred for them.
- Many active stereo speakers have all their amplification circuitry in one speaker, while the other is passive. The amplifier is calibrated for the length of cable expected between the two speakers, meaning a longer cable may make one speaker softer than the other.

Manual balance controls are a common feature in hi-fi systems and advanced OS volume settings.

Hopefully this feature can also be added to Music Assistant on a per-player basis.

When listening to radio streams that provide artwork via the ICY `StreamUrl` field (e.g., album covers from radio station APIs), Music Assistant ignores this URL entirely. Instead, it always performs a MusicBrainz lookup to find artwork, which:

- Overrides the station-provided cover with a (sometimes different) MusicBrainz result
- Adds unnecessary API calls when the stream already provides the correct artwork
- Returns no artwork at all for talk radio programs, regional stations, or lesser-known tracks that MusicBrainz doesn't index

Many radio stations (Radio France, FIP, RMC, Catalunya Radio, etc.) expose high-quality, real-time artwork through their APIs. Tools like Node-RED or custom ICY proxies can inject this artwork into `StreamUrl`, but MA currently discards it.

Parse the `StreamUrl` field from ICY metadata in `_parse_icy_metadata()` and pass it to `_update_radio_stream_metadata()` as `image_url`.

posts.excerpt:
This is a request for:

- a text configuration mechanism for Music Assistant
- a commitment to configuration-as-code as a supported aspect of the project. 

# Background

A trial of music-assistant this week to replace a 12-player multizone audio system has led to one overriding conclusion:
**UI configuration is tedious and repetitive**.

By contrast our existing multizone system runs from [a single config.json](https://github.com/markferry/multizone-audio/blob/master/example.config.json).

# Options

## Generate `settings.json`
MA `settings.json` mixes static and dynamic data which makes it unsuitable for version-control.
It is representative of the current state, not a *configuration mechanism*.

There's potential to generate `settings.json` from separate `core.json`, `providers.json`, `players.json` files.

For this a **configuration schema** would be a prerequisite.

## CLI tool and MA API

A CLI tool that interacts with the MA API (some overlap with #5355, perhaps) could be used to orchestrate configuration changes.
posts.title: Configuration as Code

**Feature Request**

Currently, the "Default enqueue option for Track item(s)" in 
Settings → System → Player Queues only offers two options:

- Play (and keep queue)
- Play (and replace queue)

**What's missing**

There is no way to set **"Play next (and keep queue)"** as the 
default action for tracks. This option exists in the track 
context menu, but it cannot be saved as a permanent default.

**Expected behavior**

The same enqueue options available in the context menu should 
also be available as default settings in Player Queue settings, 
specifically:

- Play next (and keep queue)
- Play next (and replace queue)
- Add to queue

**Why this is useful**

When listening to music and browsing for the next song, most 
users want to queue it up as "play next" rather than 
immediately interrupting playback or adding it to the very end 
of a long queue. Having to right-click every single time is 
cumbersome.

### The problem

On server startup, providers intermittently fail to load with `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files` while importing the provider module (the traceback points at reading the package `METADATA` file during import). I have seen it on the `sonos` (aiosonos) and `local_audio` (sounddevice) providers.

The server process runs with `RLIMIT_NOFILE` **soft = 1024**, hard = 524288. The soft limit of 1024 looks too low for loading all provider modules at startup. The failure is **intermittent / timing-dependent**: a restart sometimes comes up clean, sometimes not. When it happens, the affected providers stay unloaded until a later clean start — so a plain restart is not a reliable fix.

Once the server has settled, the open file descriptors of the process are low (~46), so this looks like a transient burst of open files during the concurrent provider-module import at startup crossing the 1024 soft limit, rather than a steady descriptor leak.

posts.excerpt:
### What server version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.9.1

### How is the MA server installed?

Docker Container

### The problem

Podcasts added via the Apple Podcasts (iTunes) provider fail to play — every episode is skipped with "produced no audio data". The provider stores the podcast's channel/feed URL as the per-episode stream URL (identical across all episodes; only the trailing episode id differs), so ffmpeg is handed the RSS XML and receives zero audio.

Root cause is the feed's enclosure MIME type. The episodes are valid static MP3s, but the feed (101.ru / Детское Радио) declares them as `type="file"` instead of `type="audio/mpeg"`. The provider only treats `audio/*` (or video) enclosures as playable, so it discards them and falls back to the channel/feed URL as the stream.

Repro feed: https://101.ru/getPodcast/144/120/caa409a124788ccc2ba557fd9423d068

Verified from the MA host with curl:
```
Stored stream URL  -> content-type: text/xml   (this is the RSS feed, not audio)
Enclosure mp3 URL  -> content-type: audio/mpeg, content-length: 53989776, accept-ranges: bytes (plays fine)
Feed enclosure:    <enclosure length="..." type="file" url="https://cdnN.101.ru/....mp3
posts.title: Podcast providers: enclosures with non-audio MIME (type="file") are discarded; channel feed URL used as stream URL → no audio

I have 2 cores and 6GB memory for my home assistant vm. both were running just fine, provided i kept the number of simultaneous jobs to 3. However with the upgrade it is dictating a minimum of 4 cores and 8GB ram. 

4cpu minimum is quite wasteful and seriously impacts those that run in a small virtualized environment. my entire host only has 4 cpus, requiring 1 vm to have 4vcpu causes scheduling issues and actually degrades the performance compared to fewer cpu due to cpu wait and co-scheduling issues.

### What server version of Music Assistant has the issue?

### UPDATE (18 hrs after posting)

I am going to leave this issue open for review and consideration of modifying the player protocol assignment sequence in MA.

I've worked with Claude (Opus) to analyze the MA and ESP32 concurrent log messages to identify the potential issue.

The summary of the issue:
Music Assistant may assign a player as a universal player - instead of a native protocol player - if the device was previously used in MA with a different firmware.  It comes down to a race or sequencing issue - does if find the new native protocol capability first? or does it register as a Universal Player first - and treat the newly discovered native protocol as "stale", deleting it and attempting to use a non-existent AirPlay or sendspin bridge.

What the logs seem to show:

- After changing the device firmware from Squeezelite to SendSpin, MA's Squeezelite provider attempted to find the old device with the assigned MAC address.
- Because this was now an "unknown device", the MA AirPlay provider's bridge manager created an AirPlay player and a SendSpin br

### Summary

I'd like Music Assistant to automatically power smart speakers on when playback is requested, and power them off after a configurable idle period – using the existing **Player → Power Control** feature as the underlying mechanism.

---

### Proposed Behaviour

**Auto Power On**
When a player is powered off but still configured in MA, it should remain visible in the player list rather than disappearing. When playback to that player is requested, MA should:
1. Display a brief waiting indicator
2. Trigger the configured Power Control action (e.g. turn on a HA-controlled smart plug)
3. Wait for the player to come back online and announce itself on the network
4. Start streaming as requested

**Auto Power Off**
After a configurable idle period (e.g. 1 hour of no playback activity), MA should automatically cut power to the player via the same Power Control mechanism.

---

### Use Case & Setup

I have 6 Sonos speakers of different generations used exclusively for music playback. Each consumes 3–6W at idle, totalling around **30W idle draw** even when nothing is playing.

My actual listening time is roughly 4 hours per day – meaning the speakers sit idle for ~20 hours daily.

posts.excerpt:
# Music Assistant doesn't let you pick which copy plays

When you've got the same album from more than one source — a local rip plus Qobuz, say — Music Assistant merges them into one entry and quietly decides which copy to play. That happens on the server, so it's the same no matter how you're using it: web UI, the Home Assistant integration, or your own code against the API all get whatever MA picked. There's no "use this one instead" on the merged album, and nothing tells you which copy you got unless you go dig through the queue.

The thinking behind it is "it grabs the best quality, and they're the same album anyway." The second half is where it gets shaky, and it gets shaky in exactly the cases that are easy to miss: two copies that look identical in every way you can see, but don't sound the same.

## How the pick works

It's a score. For lossless files it's basically sample rate plus bit depth, so a CD-quality 16/44 file scores 60, a 24/96 scores 120, and a 24/192 scores 216. Lossy formats score way down around 1 or 2. On top of that there's a small bonus for local files (+2, plus another +1 if the item's in your library) and for other local servers like Plex (+1); streaming

posts.excerpt:
### What server version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.8.8

### How is the MA server installed?

Home Assistant OS Addon

### The problem

In `music_assistant/controllers/players/protocol_linking.py::_check_merge_universal_players`, the merge of two `UniversalPlayer` instances with **equal** `linked_output_protocols` counts is non-deterministic across server restarts.

Current code (lines 644–650 on `dev`):

```python
# Determine which player absorbs the other (more protocols wins)
keep, remove = (
    (universal_player, player)
    if len(universal_player.linked_output_protocols)
    >= len(player.linked_output_protocols)
    else (player, universal_player)
)
```

The `>=` always keeps the caller-side `universal_player` on ties, but which side ends up as caller depends on the iteration order of `self._players.values()`, which is not stable between restarts. The merge winner therefore shuffles, and so does the surviving `player_id`.

Downstream consumers that bind by `player_id` (notably the Home Assistant integration) see entity_ids gain or lose `_2` / `_3` suffixes after every MA restart. Dashboards, automations, scripts, and HomeKit bridges that reference these entity_ids
posts.title: Non-deterministic universal player merge causes player IDs to reshuffle across server restarts

### Summary

Add a **"Not played in the last X days/weeks/months"** filter to the Smart Playlists plugin. This would exclude tracks that have been played within a configurable time window, surfacing music from your library that you haven't heard in a while.

---

### Why this is different from "No repeat within"

The existing **No repeat within** option (under Advanced) prevents the same track from appearing in consecutive evaluations of the same playlist. It's a session/queue-level deduplication tool.

The proposed filter is different in intent and scope:

| | No repeat within | Not played in X days |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | Per-playlist, tracks played recently in *that* playlist | Global play history across all sources |
| **Goal** | Avoid hearing the same song twice in a row | Surface genuinely unplayed/forgotten tracks |
| **Time window** | Hours (1–8760 h) | Days / weeks / months |
| **Use case** | Shuffle variety | Library rediscovery |

---

### Use case

Anyone with a large library knows the problem: you keep playing the same familiar tracks because they're top of mind. A huge portion of your collection sits unplayed for months or years.

A "not played in X days" filter
posts.title: Smart Playlist filter: "Not played in X days" — Library Rediscovery

### The problem

When using a Yamaha MusicCast receiver through Music Assistant with Sendspin/AirPlay as the preferred output protocol, advancing to the next track changes the parent MusicCast player's volume unexpectedly.

In this setup, the Music Assistant player `Living Room` is a Yamaha RX-V6A MusicCast player whose preferred output protocol is the Sendspin bridge for its AirPlay endpoint. On a normal `next` command, the Living Room volume dropped from 36% to 26% without any explicit volume command from Home Assistant or the user.

This looks like an AirPlay/Sendspin volume scale mismatch with the linked MusicCast parent:

- Music Assistant restarts the Sendspin/AirPlay bridge on track change.
- The bridge starts `cliraop` with `-volume 36`, copied from the parent MusicCast player's Music Assistant volume.
- The Yamaha AirPlay endpoint maps that to native MusicCast raw volume `43` out of `161`.
- Music Assistant's MusicCast provider reads that back as `int(43 / 161 * 100) == 26`.
- The parent player is then exposed as 26% volume.

The problem
Playing to a Universal Group whose member is a Squeezelite player results in a few seconds of audio followed by a hard stop. The Universal Group flow stream handler raises an unhandled KeyError while trying to read the sample_rates config of the group member, because that member is a merged universal_player and the universal_player provider does not define a sample_rates config entry.
The aiohttp request handler for the /ugp/ stream returns HTTP 500, the member's stream connection is dropped, and the player stops once its local buffer drains (hence the ~10–15 s of audio before silence).

## Feature proposal: RTL-SDR FM radio provider

I'd like to contribute a new music provider for Music Assistant named `rtlradio`.

What it does
The provider exposes user-configured FM stations as Music Assistant radio items and resolves playback to an external backend that streams audio from an RTL-SDR USB tuner.

Why external backend
The SDR-specific parts (USB device access, `rtl_fm`, `ffmpeg`, optional HA add-on packaging) remain outside Music Assistant. This keeps the provider simple and avoids introducing SDR runtime dependencies into MA itself.

 Proposed scope for initial PR
- provider folder with manifest + implementation
- config entries for backend URL and station presets JSON
- `get_library_radios`, `get_radio`, `get_stream_details`
- FM only for initial version

Explicitly out of scope
- DAB+
- autodiscovery
- RDS metadata
- backend packaging

Would this architecture be acceptable for an upstream PR?

### The problem

When two or more classic Logitech Squeezebox devices (Boom / Radio / Touch — original SqueezeOS firmware, MAC-OUI 00:04:20) are grouped for synchronised playback in MA 2.8.7, MA reports `playing` for every member, slimproto drift correction runs (skipAhead frames every few seconds), connections stay `ESTAB` for the full duration — but no audio physically comes out of the speakers. Classic SqueezeOS firmware does **not** advertise `flc` in its slimproto HELO capability list. Today, classical metadata gets squashed into the same flat "artists" list as everything else, there's no concept of a *Work* (the composition itself, separate from a particular recording), and you can't browse or search by composer. This proposal aims to fix that.

For every track and album, where the source provides it: (These are the tags as supported by MusicBrainz)

### What server version of Music Assistant has the issue?

### The problem

HTTP/2 mitigates against an entire class of vulnerabilities called "HTTP desync attack" or "HTTP smuggling". In short, this means because the backend connection between the reverse proxy and Music Assistant is shared between all users, an attacker can see content from users connecting to Music Assistant. This includes cookies, access tokens and maybe passwords.

It is not sufficient (actually has no effect) if you upgrade the frontend (between reverse proxy and web browser) connection to HTTP/2. Also, while reverse proxies try to protect against known attack vectors via regular expression hacks, new vectors come up frequently. The only known way to protect against these attacks is upgrade the backend to HTTP/2.

Music Assistant currently rejects H2C connections on port 8095 (the HTTP port):

```

music-assistant-1  | Traceback (most recent call last):

Currently, Music Assistant matches tracks [like so](https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/543):

> prefer MusicBrainz ID match or ISRC match
Album must exactly match
Title must exactly match
Version must exactly match
Fallback to duration match if both tracks have compilation (multi artist) albums

I'm currently using Navidrome to host my music collection so the "MusicBrainz ID" is provided through the OpenSubSonic API as `musicBrainzId` which is populated by the MusicBrainz Recording ID ([written to FLAC files as `MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID` by Picard](https://picard-docs.musicbrainz.org/en/latest/appendices/tag_mapping.html#id39)). 

This mostly works out well, but problems come up when a collection contains two versions of the same album (OpenSubSonic returns a `version` to Music Assistant through the API). The current logic of the (new) genre feature for local files is as follows
1. local nfo file
2. online sources such as MusicBrainz
3. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider

I personally do have my own genre matching and all my tracks therefore do have "my genres". I do not have local nfo files.

What happens is that if MusicBrainz can identify the artist properly, it will pull the genre (along with the bio and other metadata) from music brainz and I "dont want" MB's genre allocation.
I'm suggesting to change the logic to:
1. local nfo file
2. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider
3. online sources such as MusicBrainz
This would allow that you still get the bio and other items from the online metadata providers, but the genre would be propagated from the (local) tracks.

## The problem

Music Assistant registers **four parallel player bridges** for a single physical Sonos speaker (a Sonos Beam in my case) that supports multiple protocols. All four are `enabled: true` in `settings.json` out of the box, despite the [Sonos player-support docs](https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/sonos/) implying that AirPlay/DLNA variants for Sonos devices should be deduplicated.

The four concurrent bridges — each independently subscribing, probing, and keeping sessions alive — put the Sonos Beam into a sensitized state where routine network events (UPnP event subscriptions from HA, SSDP M-SEARCH responses, etc.) cascade to a media-pipeline refresh. On a Beam operating as a TV soundbar via HDMI-ARC/eARC, the media-pipeline refresh manifests as a brief ARC disconnect → TV (LG OLED in my case) retriggers its Dolby Vision handshake → "Resume playback" banner.

Ungraceful shutdown of MASS (`docker stop`) leaves residual subscription/session state on the Beam that **continues to cause the same drops at a lower frequency for many hours or until the device is factory-reset.** Factory-resetting the Beam dropped my TV-disruption rate from "every 4 minutes" to "every

posts.excerpt:
**The short story:**
It is possible that Sendspin does not work with some Chromecast devices. There is nothing we can do about this. In a future update of MA, we will automatically detect this and disable the protocol on the device.

**The long story**
To make Sendspin work with Chromecast based devices, we rely on the (bloated) implementation of the Cast protocol, which is browser based. We basically run a browser version of Sendspin inside the on-device browser of the Chromecast device. Newer devices implement the 'Google Cast for Audio (GC4A) 2.0', which is a lightweight (read non bloated) implementation that simply just does not implement the audio API's we require to run Sendspin.

This is a (non-exhaustive) list of devices that currently implement GC4A 2.0. These devices will most likely not work with Sendspin. Google aims to release this new version of Cast to more existing devices, so this list will likely grow in the future:
- Bose: Wifi Speaker and Smart Soundbars
- JBL: Charge 5 Wi-Fi / Boombox 3 Wi-Fi / Authentics 200, 300, and 500
- Samsung: Music Frame / Soundbars
- LG: Soundbars S90TY/SG10TY/SE70Q/S80Q/S90Q
- Bang & Olufsen Beosound 2 / Beocore Connect
- Sonoro Maest

cliraop starts and runs for exactly 4.1s then exits with "Audio streamer cancelled after 4.1s". shairport-sync logs show zero RTSP connection during this window despite the TCP port being reachable (verified with nc from MacBook and other devices).

MA runs inside a Docker container. The cliraop binary uses -if 192.168.0.250 (HA Pi IP) to bind its source interface. However, NO TCP packets are sent to the target device (192.168.0.45:5000), confirmed by tcpdump on the target showing zero packets from 192.168.0.250 during playback attempts. Only mDNS traffic is seen.

The MA container uses internal Docker IPs (172.17.0.1, 172.30.32.1, 172.30.232.1 visible in mDNS traffic). Binding cliraop to 192.168.0.250 from inside the container silently fails - the binary runs but sends no packets.

### The problem

This is a frontend UI/layout bug, not a playback or network issue. The mandatory troubleshooting checkboxes above don't apply — no logs, restarts, or network changes are relevant.

**Issue:** On the Discover (Home) page, the Players widget row uses a Swiper carousel with `overflow: hidden`, but provides no visual hint that more players exist beyond the visible area. If you have more players than fit on screen, the last card(s) get abruptly cut off mid-render with no navigation arrows, no scrollbar, and no fade/peek to suggest scrolling.

The media item rows below (Recently Added Tracks, Random Artists, etc.) handle this better — `Carousel.vue` uses `slides-per-view` set to count + 0.5, so there's always a half-item peeking from the right edge as a visual cue.

**Root Cause in `PlayersWidgetRow.vue`:**

The Swiper is configured with:
- `:navigation="false"` — no arrow buttons rendered
- `:free-mode="false"` — drag-scrolling snaps awkwardly on desktop
- `:slides-per-view="'auto'"` with fixed `width: 240px` per slide — no partial-item peek

**Feature Request:** 
Shuffle should optionally operate as a per-session or per-queue setting rather than always being a persistent player-level state that survives across separate playback sessions.

**Currently**
When shuffle is enabled on a Music Assistant player — whether via the UI or via media_player.shuffle_set in a HA automation — it is set persistently on that player. It remains enabled regardless of what is played next, even if the queue is fully replaced via enqueue: replace. This means:
	∙	Enable shuffle for a morning playlist automation at 5:45 AM
	∙	Hours later, open MA and play Abbey Road with “replace queue”
	∙	Abbey Road plays in shuffled order, not track sequence

The shuffle state carries over even though the intent was clearly a fresh, unrelated playback session.

**My Feelings/Request**
Shuffle feels fundamentally different from other persistent player settings like volume or repeat. Volume persisting makes intuitive sense — you expect your speaker to remember how loud it was. But shuffle is tied to what you’re playing and why, not to the speaker itself. I would suspect most users expect shuffle to be a property of a playback session, not a permanent characteri

posts.excerpt:
## Summary

`SyncGroupPlayer` is a virtual abstraction representing a sync group as a single entity for UI, volume control, and plugin interaction. However, throughout the codebase, it is **not** treated interchangeably with physical players. Instead, numerous call sites contain special-case logic that checks player type, player ID prefix, or `sync_leader` attributes to bridge the gap between the physical and logical layers.

This creates a recurring pattern where every new feature that interacts with players must independently discover and work around the fact that sync groups are a different beast -- leading to subtle bugs (see [PR music-assistant/server#3512](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3512) for a concrete example with plugin volume callbacks).

**Goal:** At all but the lowest-level physical transport/plugin layer, a `SyncGroupPlayer` should be 100% interchangeable with an individual physical player. Most providers and controllers should not need to know or care whether they are operating on a sync group or an individual player.

## The Core Gap: `in_use_by` and Plugin Source Ownership

The `PluginSource.in_use_by` field (defined in `models/plugin.py`) holds

posts.excerpt:
Music-assistant (MA) players relies on players being on auto-discovered on the same subnet/VLAN, which creates a conflict when installed as an addon for HA. 

Using an isolated subnet/VLAN for wifi-enabled smart devices is quite commonly recommended security practice. For a lot of home-assistant (HA) addons it is required to have HA on the same subnet as said devices. Shelly, ESPHome etc but also the products that are cloud connected and a black box on your network.

Multimedia devices are a middle-of-the-road thing where you sort of have to trust them on your regular network if you want to be able to easily connect and cast to them, possibly restricted by some firewall rules if you are ambitious with security. 

So the current solution is to use the HA Mediaplayer provider with HA as a proxy to the device. It works... ish. But as the MA documentation for Home Assistant Media Players states multiple times, it is very much not recommended, and using a native player in MA is preferred.

In conclusion, it would make sense for MA to allow for manual configuration of players alongside with the auto discovery feature.

### The problem

When MA's cache controller raises `TypeError: default serializer exceeds recursion limit` (https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4807 - closed as not planned), it does not silently drop the failed cache write. Instead it resets the active playback queue, causing playback to stop completely.
 
- The interruption is triggered by an AirPlay bridge device registration event for my laptop `CA11020656` (bridge `apaac009bf1655` / `spb_aac009bf1655`), which appears to cause a cascade of cache serialization failures
- The cache failure corrupts the in-memory queue state for the Front Bedroom player, causing `player_queues` to abandon the current queue and re-fetch from playlog
- The playlog resume is logged as `userid + queue_id match`, meaning the same queue ID is retained — but playback is still interrupted while tracks are re-fetched
- This is a silent failure in HA's logbook (no automation or service call is logged as the cause), making it very difficult to diagnose without MA's own logs

posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.8.1

### How is the MA server installed?

Home Assistant OS Addon

### The problem

Two related issues when playing to a JBL Authentics 300:

**Issue 1: AirPlay is selected despite Chromecast being the preferred protocol**

The JBL supports both AirPlay and Chromecast. Despite setting `preferred_output_protocol` to the Chromecast player ID, MA consistently selects AirPlay. AirPlay then fails (playback starts but never produces audio).

Root cause: the JBL has `cast_type=None` because `pychromecast.dial` fails to determine the cast type (TLS handshake timeout on the device info endpoint). This makes Chromecast discovery slow (~2 minutes after startup). During this time, AirPlay is already available, and since `PROTOCOL_PRIORITY` ranks AirPlay (10) higher than Chromecast (30), the fallback always picks AirPlay.

The `preferred_output_protocol` setting is ignored because the Chromecast protocol player is still `available: False` when play is triggered:
```
DEBUG  Recovered cached protocol link up843e1d257560 -> d7223586-... (available: False)
DEBUG  Starting playback on Enceinte JBL via protocol Airplay  <- should be Chromecast
```
posts.title: JBL Authentics 300: Chromecast STREAM_TYPE_BUFFERED causes stream reset after ~12MB; AirPlay fallback due to slow Cast discovery

I have 2 older uPNP players which don't allow you to Pause live streams - they just ignore the Pause command when the source is a stream.  This means MA thinks it's paused the music and is in "paused" state, but the music is still playing.  In the Lyrion Music Server (aka Squeezebox) uPNP Bridge plugin this is solved by providing an option to replace Pause with Stop if the source is a stream.  The description is 

```
<live_pause>0 | 1</live_pause > default = 1

Some players will not pause when playing live streams (e.g.webradio). It’s correct that although you can buffer or “timeshift” livestream, in most case it does not make sense as gap with real time increases forever, at every pause. For such players, the bridge can commute LMS’ pause request into a stop (only when playing a livestream)
```

I wondered if it would be possible to add a similar option to the uPNP provider

**Describe the bug**
When the Music Assistant HA integration is reloaded — whether triggered by an HA restart, a manual integration reload, or the MA server restarting — the HA entity IDs for Music Assistant media players change unpredictably. ### The problem

I was delighted to see a new release of MA this afternoon. However, I was not so happy to see that, despite 2.8.0 being numbered  a minor release under [SemVer](https://semver.org/#spec-item-7), there was a big warning at the top of the release notes (I'm glad I glanced at them!) saying that this release does, in fact, include breaking changes. This undermines the purpose of using SemVer, in my opinion—I believe that *any* breaking change should increment the major counter so that users can more effectively gauge the amount of research they should do before upgrading. Contrary to how some projects operate, a "major release" shouldn't have to mean major changes were made—simply breaking changes. Check out Tom Preston-Werner's ["Major Version Numbers are Not Sacred"](https://tom.preston-werner.com/2022/05/23/major-version-numbers-are-not-sacred) for a much more qualified argument about why breaking changes should always be major releases. posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.6.6

### How is the MA server installed?

Docker Container

### The problem

Im trying to create a Bluetooth A2DP to Webradio Bridge on a raspberry PI with claude code.  It works well. But it has a great delay.
 
Claude identified the following problem. I hope this is not ai slop and is really the cause for my delay.

The following is completely written by claude:

## Description

  When playing a radio stream (added via URL) on a Squeezelite/slimproto player,
  there is a consistent ~8 second delay before playback starts. The same stream
  in VLC starts in ~1 second. 

  ## Root Cause (identified)

  The slimproto `play_url` call uses `threshold=200` (200 KB) for radio streams.
  At 192 kbps = 24 KB/s, Squeezelite must buffer 200 KB before firing `STMl`
  (BUFFER_READY), which takes **~8.3 seconds**.

  This is confirmed in the MA source — `_patched_send_strm` already uses
  `threshold=64` for plugin sources (introduced in PR #3018), but radio streams
  (`MediaType.RADIO`) receive the default `threshold=200` from aioslimproto.

## Steps to Reproduce

  1. Add any radio stream URL in Music Assistant
  2. Play it on a Squeezelite
posts.title: Radio streams have ~8s startup delay with Squeezelite players due to hardcoded threshold=200

### The problem

Sorting favorite tracks by "Recently Added" (or `timestamp_added`) does not work correctly for providers that do not supply a `date_added` field. All tracks end up with `timestamp_added = 0` in the database, so sorting by date added silently falls back to alphabetical order.

**Affected providers:** Deezer, Spotify, Jellyfin, and others that do not set `date_added` during parsing.

**Working providers:** Tidal (uses `created` field), filesystem_local (uses file modification time).

**API evidence (Deezer, 28 favorite tracks):**

```
GET music/tracks/library_items {favorite: true, limit: 30}
```

Response returns tracks in alphabetical order (Achilles, Appoloduction, A Song for You, Assez...) with no `date_added` or `timestamp_added` field present.

The sorting order is identical regardless of whether `order_by: "timestamp_added"` or `order_by: "timestamp_added_desc"` is specified, confirming all values are the same (0).

**Root cause (from source analysis):**

In `controllers/media/tracks.py` line 536:

```python
"timestamp_added": int(item.date_added.

## Problem

When a Sendspin bridge client reconnects (e.g. after a version upgrade or hostname change), the player's `device_info` (model/product_name, manufacturer, software_version) is not updated in Music Assistant — MA continues showing the old values.

## Root Cause

In `music_assistant/providers/sendspin/provider.py` ([source](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/main/music_assistant/providers/sendspin/provider.py)), `_handle_client_added()` calls `self.mass.players.register(player)` which raises `AlreadyRegisteredError` if the player is already registered. There is also an early check:

```python
if self.mass.players.get_player(client_id) is not None:
    self.logger.debug("Client %s already registered, skipping duplicate add event", client_id)
    return
```

When a bridge restarts, the sendspin client reconnects before MA processes `ClientRemovedEvent` (TCP keepalive timeout is slower than reconnect). The old player is still registered → new `SendspinPlayer` with fresh `DeviceInfo` is skipped entirely.

Hello, I recently was trying to make a ESP32 based small screen to show the album artwork playing on the music assistant.
In the debug log, I noticed one thing.

I used a homeassistant text_sensor to obtain the entity_picture attribute from home assistant. When I switch from a playing track to another. I first get an URL and in a few milliseconds get another one.
The first URL is pointing to the last artwork url, and second is the one to new url. Furthermore, they are in different string combinations.
I looked in MA log. I guess I found the reason.
The first URL is generated by metadata.py including provider+image_format+size=500+path. And the second URL is generated by images.py including path+provider+size=0.

In my use case I need to ignore the first one and only download the picture from the second url which is for the new track.

I would like to ask if this is intended, and I was thinking to skip the first one by searching for "fmt=" string or "size=500" string, because new url doesn't contains that. I hope this will be not be changed in future and cause my code issue :)

## Summary

Add an Overcast podcast provider that imports subscriptions and played status from [Overcast](https://overcast.fm), the popular iOS podcast app by Marco Arment.

Overcast exposes user data through an authenticated extended OPML export that includes podcast subscriptions (with RSS feed URLs) and per-episode played/progress state. This is enough to build a read-only podcast provider that auto-discovers a user's subscriptions and imports their listening history.

## Why Overcast?

- One of the most popular podcast apps on iOS
- Already exposes structured data: the extended OPML export at `/account/export_opml/extended` includes RSS feed URLs, episode GUIDs, played status, and progress timestamps
- Users migrating to Music Assistant for home audio want their existing podcast library to follow them without manually re-adding each show
- The existing `podcastfeed` provider handles single feeds well, but Overcast users often have 20-50+ subscriptions — a provider that bulk-imports from their account would close that gap

## Proposed Implementation

### Authentication
- Email/password login via `POST https://overcast.fm/login` (session cookie auth)
- No official API exists, so

posts.excerpt:
Hey everyone,
I (and probably many others) run home assistant virtualized in Proxmox. The default processor type (kvm64) does not support the new numpy version, which leads to music assistant not starting without a clear error (just a cryptic `NumPy was built with baseline optimizations:  (X86_V2) but your machine doesn't support: (X86_V2)`, see https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5005).
This can be very easily fixed by changing the CPU type of the VM, and I feel like it could be a time-saver for many people to include a short note like this in the update notes, if possible:

> [!WARNING]
> This update introduces a dependency update, which renders Music Assistant unusable on very old cpus (which also includes the Proxmox default `kvm64`).
> Before updating, please make sure your CPU (virtualized or not) supports the X86_V2 instruction set.
> Proxmox users can most likely just set the processor type to `x86-64-v2-AES`.
> For more information, see https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5005.

Thank you for your consideration, and for developing such a great project! :)

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.7.8

### How is the MA server installed?

Docker Container

### The problem

When the same audiobook title exists in Audiobookshelf as multiple distinct recordings with different narrators, Music Assistant merges all recordings into a single library item returned by music/audiobooks/library_items.

The merged item:
- Retains only one narrator name, discarding the others
- Concatenates the chapter lists from all recordings, producing a doubled or otherwise incorrect chapter count
- Exposes all underlying Audiobookshelf item UUIDs via provider_mappings, but no MA API endpoint returns the correct per-recording metadata for each UUID

As a result, clients cannot surface multiple narrator versions to users. In testing with a library containing both a Stephen Fry and a Jim Dale narration of the same Harry Potter titles, only 8 library items are returned where 16 distinct recordings exist.

Verified: calling the Audiobookshelf HTTP API directly for each UUID in provider_mappings returns the correct narrator and chapter count per recording. The merge is applied by Music Assistant, not Audiobookshelf.

posts.excerpt:
Hello,

I've started working on a PoC implementing a mechanism that will allow users to block specific tracks or artists so they are automatically skipped during playback. This is particularly useful for provider auto-generated playlists, like radio-generated queues.

Before I finalize the implementation, I wanted to check if this aligns with the project vision and get your input.

Player Behavior:
- Blocked items are silently skipped
- If currently playing item gets blocked → immediate skip
- If no unblocked items remain in queue → graceful stop

**Implementation Plan**

1. Models

    Add blocked: bool = False attribute to:
    - Track dataclass
    - Artist dataclass

2. Server - Database & Controllers

    - Add blocked column to tracks and artists tables
    - Add set_blocked(item_id, blocked) method to TracksController and ArtistsController
    - Update queries to include blocked field

3. Server - API Commands

    Add to MusicController:
    - music/blocked/add_item - Block track or artist
    - music/blocked/remove_item - Unblock track or artist
    - music/blocked/items - List all blocked items

4. Server - Playback Logic
  
    Modify PlayerQueuesController._play_index()

In my setup (Music Assistant + Snapcast), the audio output is delayed due to buffering and network latency, while lyrics are displayed based on server-side timing. This causes lyrics to appear ahead of the audible audio.

I know that Music Assistant can’t know the exact moment audio reaches the speakers, especially with buffered transports like Snapcast, so perfect sync isn’t realistic.
However, a configurable lyrics timing offset (in ms) would still be very useful.

Ideally:
- a static offset value
- configurable globally and/or per player
- applied only to lyrics rendering

Even an approximate offset would already improve usability a lot in setups with a mostly consistent playback delay.

Thanks!

## Problem
Currently, Music Assistant only supports built-in username/password authentication and Home Assistant OAuth. For users running their own authentication systems (like Authentik, Authelia, or Keycloak), there's no way to integrate these with Music Assistant.

This means:
- Every user needs to create and manage separate credentials for Music Assistant
- No centralized user management
- Can't leverage existing SSO infrastructure
- No MFA enforcement from identity provider

## Proposed Solution
Add support for generic OpenID Connect authentication providers (like Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, Auth0, etc.)

**User experience:**
1. Admin configures OIDC provider details in Music Assistant settings (provider URL, client ID, client secret)
2. Users see "Login with [Provider Name]" button on login page
3. Click button → redirect to identity provider → authenticate → redirect back to Music Assistant
4. User is automatically logged in (and created if first time)

**Benefits:**
- Easy user onboarding - users can login with their existing accounts
- Centralized user management
- Support for MFA via identity provider
- Works with popular self-hosted solutions like Authentik
- Single l

2.8.0b3

### The problem

_**In these cases I have excluded use in flow mode.**_

**Issue 1: Skipped tracks caused by premature HTTP disconnect during prefetch
Description**

Denon DLNA renderers intentionally close HTTP connections after partially downloading a track, typically during prefetch / probing of the next item.
This is valid DLNA behavior for file-based servers.

Music Assistant, however, acts as a hybrid streaming/transcoding proxy, not a static file server, and currently interprets such early disconnects as premature stream failures.

As a result:

MA logs warnings like

Player <Denon> disconnected prematurely from stream sent X bytes, expected Y bytes

In some cases MA marks the preloaded queue item as failed
When transition occurs, MA skips the preloaded track and advances to the following one
This leads to randomly skipped tracks, especially noticeable with Denon players.

Important clarification
This is not a Denon bug.

Denon behaves correctly for a DLNA file-based model:

- it may download part of a file
- close the connection
- reopen later or switch URI at

I historically have operated a Librespot server in my IoT network and leveraged the [ZeroConf API](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/commercial-hardware/implementation/guides/zeroconf) of Spotify Connect using the [Librespot Zeroconf argument](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/issues/91). This allows me to predictably use an mDNS repeater to announce the Spotify Connect messages to my user VLANs, and then have them respond over the advertised port, which is preconfigured to use whatever is configured via the Librespot Zeroconf argument. 

For example, if I configure Librespot to use TCP port 42069, and the IP address of my Librespot server is 192.168.5.1, I configure two flows and one service on my firewall:
- Service: mDNS Repeater or equivalent between my IoT zone and my Users zone;
- One inbound firewall flow for traffic from my IoT zone destined for my Users zone which permits mDNS messages (224.0.0.251:5353); and
- One inbound firewall flow for traffic from my Users zone destined for my IoT zone which permits the TCP session establishment between the Spotify Client and the Spotify Connect server (192.168.5.1:42069).

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.7.2

### How is the MA server installed?

Home Assistant OS Addon

### The problem

I have the following setup that works without issue using MA 2.6.3 - Music Assistant running as an Add On in a HAOS VM. Reverse proxy that adds SSL via pfSense/HAProxy and a public domain, which is used for all HA/MA access.

Upgrading to 2.7.0 and/or 2.7.1 introduces an issue with maintaining a connection via the web socket (per Chrome console). If idling at a library page, every 30-60 seconds, the connection will get dropped and the page will refresh. Same thing happens if music is playing via the browser - music drops/stops upon the refresh.

I have tested the following scenarios:
Direct to HAOS IP:MA port - Works without issue,
Setting HAProxy to music.homedomain.com and directing to HAOS IP: MA port - same problem as above.,
Opening via the homeassistant domain via the Add Ons Ingress also presents the issue.

Provider should handle missing optional metadata fields gracefully by using sensible defaults (e.g., channels=2 for stereo, sample_rate=44100, bit_depth=16).

# Apple Music Authentication Issue - SOLVED ✅

## Root Cause Identified

**THE APP TOKEN IS EXPIRED!** 🚨

- **App Token Expired**: October 21, 2025 (3 days ago)
- **Current Date**: October 24, 2025
- **Your User Token**: Valid format, but cannot work without valid app token

3. **Your User Token**: Format is correct, but it cannot authenticate without a valid app token

The authentication chain requires BOTH tokens:
- App Token (JWT) - Authenticates the application with Apple
- User Token - Authenticates the user's Apple Music account

When the app token expires, NO user tokens will work, regardless of their validity.

## Immediate Solution
