posts.excerpt:
I'd like to propose a change to how the footer Play controls bar works throughout Music Assistant.

Currently, the bar operates as a floating island at the bottom of the screen, with the content sliding underneath it, and the scroll bar for the main page content (on desktop) also floating underneath it.

This is problematic for a couple reasons, first the inaccessibility of the scrollbar controls at the bottom of the scrollable area (users cannot click the arrows if their system uses them, or operate the scroll track if it's underneath the play bar). Secondly, it hides content that is underneath it and in some cases makes it less accessible and clickable (I have in some cases navigated to a situation where controls were underneath the playback bar, and I could not use them; I had to resize the window in order to manipulate the UI into making these controls clickable).

Philosophically, the nature of the controls bar being "floating" implies it's more of an ephemeral control, and results in a slightly more complex feel, as content interacts with it underneath and around. This extra complexity isn't really necessary or beneficial, and the difference in look and feel is not all that m

**Update:** Specification and implementations of Resonate has been renamed to “***Sendspin***” (i.e. “Sendspin Protocol” “Sendspin Server/Client”):

* https://www.sendspin-audio.com/

  * https://github.com/Sendspin/spec

**Update!** Music Assistant server now have built-in native support for Sendspin that is enabled by default as an official technical-preview from the Open Home Foundation and development of its server and client implementations are moving very fast:

* https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/sendspin/

    [00:02.50]This is the second line.
    ```

While I really enjoy using Music Assistant—and now that we have Spotify Connect—it’s still a bit of a shame that Plexamp Headless is not available yet as a plugin provider. The UI of Music Assistant is definitely improving, but to be fair, nothing currently comes close to the Plexamp mobile experience. It would be amazing if Music Assistant players could function as headless Plexamp receivers.

Sure, we can stream our Plex library through Music Assistant, but it’s just not the same as casting directly from the Plexamp app. The mobile experience is truly exceptional.

I’d be very grateful if Plexamp Headless could be implemented as a plugin provider, allowing all players to act as headless receivers for Plexamp, just as with Spotify Connect. I don’t have the technical knowledge to say how feasible that is—it sounds simple in theory, but I imagine there are many technical details I might be overlooking that could make implementation more complex.

Keep up the great work!

As all of this done in the background there is no way for the users to know if any of this is happening at all.
Some of that info may be gleaned from logging info, but that only happens when there's critical issues and few users would look at logging info under normal circumstances.

```
`2025-04-24 15:55:17.432 WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.snapcast] {'code': -32603, 'data': 'Stream with name "Music Assistant - ugpegnamzuq" already exists', 'message': 'Internal error'}`
```

Notes:
- The snapcast provider re-uses existing streams, so we would expect that it wouldn't try to create two with the same name. However, the two streams are created simultaneously, leaving no time to update the list of streams, so the provider does not detect that the stream already exists.
- Even if the stream were re-used by both players it still would be problematic for universal groups with dynamic players. If one of the players is removed from the group it will delete the stream although it is still being used by the other player.

I discovered this while preparing a PR for a new feature. I will submit

posts.excerpt:
pacmd is handy to stream sound from one linux to another since it's in most repos and on desktops.
I use it to stream sound from Ubuntu VMs with Spotify to Rpi's connected to speakers all over the house.

The pacmd server runs on the Rpi and the client connects to it via:
pacmd load-module module-tunnel-sink server=SERVERIP:port

It creates a dummy sound card on the client machine.
Sound quality is good (PCM), it's reliable and it doesn't require any extra software besides what's in the distro already.

So Music assistant just needs to invoke the command above to connect to a remote pacmd server.

*On the Rpi side (or any computer connected to the speakers/amp) you run the command bellow to listen to the streams (or use the Pulsaudio extended GUI):
pactl load-module module-native-protocol-tcp port=PORT listen=SERVERIPADDRESS auth-ip-acl='127.0.0.1;CLIENTIP' auth-anonymous=1

SERVERIP=IP of Rpi player
CLIENTIP=IP of the MusicAssistant.

It would be fantastic to have the ability to specify a local soundcard as an audio output for a player. This feature would effectively turn Music Assistant into a full-fledged open-source wired multi-room audio system.

To elaborate, I have a multi-room audio player from a company called CasaTunes, which is essentially a low-spec PC with two physical soundcards. Each output of these soundcards represents a zone (or room) and acts as an independent player. There are other companies employing the same approach while charging unreasonably high prices for it.

The idea of implementing local players would simply require the ability to specify the device and subdevice, for example:
```-a hw:1,0```

This enhancement would open up new possibilities for multi-room audio setups using wired connections, adding tremendous flexibility for users.

posts.excerpt:
Hi! I'm using Music Assistant in Home Assistant to stream music to a receiver (Onkyo, DLNA). The MA volume slider controls the receiver's volume setting directly, but setting it below 30 is inaudible, and above 60 is dangerously loud. I've had users accidentally change the volume way too high with the slider, as they are accustomed to 0=not audible, 1=barely audible, 100=loud but not deadly. I didn't find any way to change the limits in MA or HA - HA Onkyo DLNA integration lets me set a maximum volume but the setting is not used by MA, and MA's volume normalization can be used to restrict the max volume, but then the receiver needs to be turned very high to hear anything, which is again dangerous when switching to another source. Apologies if this exists or doesn't belong in MA & thanks for the great app!

In summary: a per-output setting that changes what volumes 0 and 100 map to in the volume slider.

_Submitting per recommendation by @MarvinSchenkel [on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/753947050995089438/1242741503642570752/1295994774918266881)_

Some music providers allow playlists to be organized into playlist folders, which greatly improves organization.  It would be useful to have the same concept supported in Music Assistant.  

Currently, Music Assistant 'flattens' all of a provider's playlists into a single level both within the Playlist and Browse views.  I would like to propose that at least the Browse view provide support for navigating a provider's playlist folder hierarchy if it has one.

In my current system, my Apple Music subscription contains over a thousand playlists, many with the same names.  By organizing them into folders, it is easier to impose my own navigation system to quickly find what I am looking for.  It has also eliminated the confusion of having many playlists with the same name at the same level of the hierarchy, and not knowing which playlist is which.

### The problem

When playing any queued music (i.e., album, playlist), songs are skipped.  Playback can also be stuttered or stopped.
This occurs with YouTube Music and Sonos.

### How to reproduce

1.  Open MusicAssistant
2. Search for any album. See Album Details.  Example:  Miles Davis - Kind of Blue., 
3. Select from drop down, Play Now (clear queue).

Media Position is not synchronized correctly or updated frequently enough between MusicAssistant (MA) and HomeAssistant (HASS). 

When adjusting the position of the current track in the MA web UI using the progress slider, the position is sometimes not transmitted to HASS or is not transmitted correctly. The same problem also exists the other way around.

Since the media_position is not updated regularly, it is only estimated in HASS based on the timestamp (media_position_updated_at), and there may be discrepancies between the progress indicator in HASS and MA.

It would probably be more robust to synchronize progress at a minimum interval of 10 seconds, for example.

Change the progress bar in mediaplayer states via the Web-UI of MA or HASS and observe the reaction on the other side.

posts.excerpt:
As far as I can tell, Music Assistant currently uses ffmpeg's `loudnorm` filter to do loudness normalization. I'm unclear when that calculation is done (on demand? on import?), but it's a relatively cpu-heavy filter to run, and while the loudnorm filter's one-pass support for dynamic normalization (dynamic range compression, effectively) might be useful for radio or podcast streams, the filter is not always appropriate for local music files. (Note that for determining the integrated loudness of local files, ffmpeg's `ebur128` filter should run faster.)

But all of my music files contain pre-calculated "integrated" loudness adjustment information, stored either in the form of [ReplayGain 2.0 tags](https://wiki.hydrogenaud.io/index.php?title=ReplayGain_2.0_specification) or [Opus R128 Gain tags](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7845.html#section-5.2.1). It would be great if Music Assistant could retrieve and use this precalculated loudness normalization information, rather than do its own loudness calculations. (Note that the ReplayGain 2.0 tags use a reference level of -18 LUFS, while the Opus R128 tags use a reference level of -23 LUFS.)

Ideally, the ability to select whether to
posts.title: Use ReplayGain (and Opus R128 Gain) tags for loudness normalization

posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.1.0

### What version of the Home Assistant Integration have you got installed?

2024.6.2

### The problem

Requests to the LLM to control media players are unreliable and slow.
Debugging reveals that they often make multiple calls to the custom intent, with the first erroring, after using the `query` key. Later if it retries using the `track` or `artist` key it succeeds. If the same conversation agent is configured in MA then the calls to the API initiated by MA will confuse the conversation.

### How to reproduce

Configure chat GPT, use the 3.5 model and ask it to play a track with debug logging turned on.

### Music Providers

Spotify
RadioBrowser

### Player Providers

Cast devices via mass

Hi,

I've recently discovered CATT (https://github.com/skorokithakis/catt) and had started writing a web-based media service to allow Google Nest Hub devices to play media file from the local LAN.

Then my husband pointed me to Music Assistant Server and it looked like it could save a lot of time as it has support for both ChromeCast and local and SMB file storage.

The major stumbling blocks, unfortunately, have been:
- recognising media file types -- such as mkv
- transcoding media file types for playback based on the supported media types of the rendering device

CATT provides much wider support - based on ffmpeg, I believe.

With both Music Assistant Server and CATT written in python, I was wondering if there could be any synergistic development between the two projects that would overcome the above (and possibly other) current limitations in Music Assistant Server and speed its development.

Thanks,

-- Peter

posts.excerpt:
Currently, the players in the settings / player list are sorted by alphabetical order.
This is not ideal when there are numerous disabled players,that still show up in the middle of the list. The only way to hide them is to delete the corresponding provider, but that's often not suitable - thus the existence of the "disable" feature on individual players.

I propose a simple change to show two lists, first the enabled players, followed by some separator line, followed by the list of disabled players.
A possible alternative would be some sort of toggle button to switch between the lists of enabled and disabled players.

The next proposal concerns groups. Currently, there is no visual distinction between Airplay groups and other players, for example. This makes them hard to locate in a long player list. The same issue exists for Chromecast groups - one can't tell them apart from individual players.
Universal groups already have their own icon. I'm not sure what the difference should look like. It could be a different background color for the icon. Or there could be a separate column in the view indicating that the device is a group. Or the player type string should include the inform

posts.excerpt:
Once upon a time, the Google Home app supported casting the Android device device audio to a group of Chromecast devices - or Chromecast audio devices in my case. Then, Sonos sued Google, and they removed this functionality from their app. It still supports redirecting the device audio (or screen), but only to a single Chromecast devices, and no longer to a group.

My main use case is to cast audio from a Youtube music video playing in Firefox with an ad blocker, and casting that to more than one room at a  time, say a whole floor, or the whole house. I'm aware that in this case, the audio and video are out of sync, but that's not a concern at all since I'm not even looking at the screen, and the phone may even be locked while I listen.

It should be noted that even using all-Google software (say, Youtube app, Youtube Music app, or Chrome, and the Google Home app) there is no way to accomplish this, even to a single Chromecast device, let alone a group, as far as I know. The Youtube app can only cast to Chromecast video devices, not Chromecast audio. This is probably due to A/V sync reasons. Every time I open up Music Assistant I have to select the player I want.  For me personally, 99% of the time this is the same player for me, the kitchen speaker.

I'd love an option I can tick in Players that's "Make this Player the default selection" or similar, and if ticked, by default when Music Assistant is opened and would, at present say "No Player Selected" the Player with "Make this Player the default selection" ticked would be automatically selected.

I understand that having a default player selected was an option previously but that this then meant a number of users ended up having music playing on a device they didn't mean to.  Thus the default out-of-the-box experience should be as it is today, no default is selected.  My feature request only suggests providing the ability to select (And it should also be possible to untick the default, reverting to the current behaviour)

Thank you very much for considering (or not!) this request.

Tim

1. Make sure you have, for example, port 9000 occupied.

Note that this discussion will be updated (including the attached files) as HA core updates occur. (Updated for HA 2026.6.0 All Volume, Mute, Pause, Resume, Previous and Next intents removed. Improvements have been made to attempt to mimic HA's capability to identify the correct player when targetting an area)

HA supports the commands of NEXT, PREVIOUS, PAUSE, UNPAUSE, MUTE and VOLUME when targeted at a specific player or to an area. The PLAY command must be supported by the user a [blueprint is available in a dedicated repository](https://github.com/music-assistant/voice-support). For the remaining [service calls](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/media_player/) (including targetting areas) you can use custom sentences. Note that targetting an area which has multiple players may result in unpredictable behaviour although for Clear Queue and Stop the player that is in the state of `playing` will be targeted.  

Firstly add this file to \\\YOUR_HA_IP\config\custom_sentences\en
[media.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30727410/media.yaml)

Of course you can change this file to reflect your language and change the `en` in the file path accordingly. Please share

2.0.0b106

### What version of the Home Assistant Integration have you got installed?

2024.2.0

### The problem

As per title, when streaming to Snapcast clients, every songs stops playing ~10 seconds before the end of the track. By "stops playing" I mean that the web UI shows the track still playing, but no sound is reproduced.

### How to reproduce

Play a song using a Snapcast player.

### Music Providers

Filesystem (local disk)

### Player Providers

Snapcast

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Additional information

I tried to debug the problem and took a look at the Snapcast provider code, and this is what I found:

As soon as execution hits line 300 of file `music_assistant/server/providers/snapcast__init.py__`, function `play_media`, Snapcast server stop sending audio to all clients. This line is reached when all pcm chunks are sent to the Snapcast stream (the tcp socket automatically created by Music Assistant with name `MusicAssistant--{port}`). The problem is that, by this time, Snapcast still has some bytes left to send to its clients, but whent it sees the stream being destroyed it stops sending them.

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2024.1.0

### The problem

Nextcloud Music plugin provides subsonic API, but Music Assistant cannot communicate with it because Nextcloud does not provide Subsonic MD5 token-based authentication. (it seems they decided to [use SHA-256 to store the token](https://github.com/owncloud/music/blob/master/lib/Middleware/SubsonicMiddleware.php#L118) instead of MD5, which is broken decades ago. Also, TLS being omnipresent in these days, so "legacy" authentication is no longer a security risk anyway)

### How to reproduce

1. Set up the Nextcloud instance with the music plugin.
2. In Nextcloud Music settings, create a new subsonic credential.
3. Attempt to use that credential on Music Assistant Subsonic Music provider
4. Watch it fail with the "Token authentication not supported" error message.

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Additional information

Exposing configuration UI to set value passed to `legacyAuth=[bool]` https://github.com/khers/py-opensonic/blob/master/src/libopensonic/connection.py#46 to user interface will solve the problem.

Relevant codes:
https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/main/music_assistant/se

posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.0.0b88

### The problem

This has been around in at least the last 3 beta versions (since I started testing MA again for v2.0.0b85), and still exists in b88.

If your queues have anything in them, but are NOT playing/connected to speakers (GHome/chromecast in my case), and you send a TTS to a speaker, MA will begin playing back the queue for that speaker or group.

It does this even with Auto Play/Power On disabled. Individual speakers or groups will exhibit the same behavior respectively. The only way to prevent the issue is to completely empty the queue for the device or group. Even then, MA still assumes connection to the speaker after TTS plays and just sits Idle.

Ideally, if MA isn't already playing, it should never connect to and start playback after a TTS, even with Auto Play enabled. 

Of course, if music was already playing and a TTS comes in, it should play the TTS and then resume the music. This functionality DOES work, but perhaps a little too well. 🤣

### How to reproduce

1. send a TTS, for example:
````
service: tts.cloud_say
data:
  entity_id: media_player.den_speaker
  message: The Front Door has been unlocked.

### The problem

When using multiple filesystem entries the removal of some entries does not seem to be handled correctly. 

If the remaining filesystem entries are non-consecutive based on the initial time they were added, for example:

~~1~~2
1~~2~~3
1~~23~~4
1~~2~~3~~4~~

Adding a new filesystem entry will simply replace the last filesystem entry that already exists. So in case of the last example entry 3 is replaced by the new entry.

Restoring the consecutive order or completely removing all entries fixes things, so:

12~~3~~4 Adding replaces entry 4
12~~34~~ Adding creates new entry 3

Most AV receivers and renderer support 24 bit audio as Flac or WAV stream.
It would be great to have an option to choose between 16 and 24 bit output and processing to avoid loss in dynamic resolution when volume normalization is active.

@marcelveldt gave some very interesting insights in how audio is handled inside music assistant #1501 :

> All tracks are processed as raw pcm by Music Assistant internally. So everything you play will be first converted to just raw pcm in the sample rate and bit depth of the origin (unless flow mode is enabled) and the gain adjustment is done while extracting the raw source media so the pcm chunks we get into the streaming engine have the gain adjustment applied, that way there should be enough headroom withit the 16 or 24 bits sample rate. ... I settled on applying the correction gain while extracting the raw audio from its base codec. ...
> The final part in the chain is that MA sends either the raw pcm data to the player or encodes it into a codec of the user's choice, by default this is FLAC due to it being lossless while keeping a sane file size ...

In the current implementation, every single protocol's scanner returns a distinct playback device entity. This can result in multiple entries for the same device over different protocols, which can be quite annoying in a mixed-protocol environment.

For example, I have a number of Sonos speakers, SOME of them with AirPlay2 support, a number of Apple HomePods, a Samsung soundbar that supports both DLNA and AirPlay2, which is connected to a Philips TV that also supports DLNA, with Chromecast...

The result is a quite noisy list of devices where it's hard to pick which one I want to play on. 

For this reason, I'd like to recommend a merge logic for these speakers.

The first step would be merging ALL devices under the same IP address. If a Sonos speaker responds to both Sonos and DLNA and AirPlay2, don't create three entries, but rather one entry, with a list of protocols supported, and then when playback is initiated, use the most fitting backend.

An additional step would be filtering devices based on name, and if a non-unique name is found, attaching the device model/manufacturer behind it. In my case, both my Apple TV (which has two HomePods in Home Theatre mode connected), and m

### The problem

The vuetify config file loaded through the [vite config](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/vite.config.ts#L22) is currently used to [load the full content](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/src/styles/settings.scss#L12) of the global.css stylesheet, and the styles from '@egjs/vue3-flicking`. 

It's not intended to do this ([vuetify docs](https://vuetifyjs.com/en/features/sass-variables/#duplicated-css)) as this leads to a copy of these styles being injected into every single component, causing lots of duplicated code.

A preferred solution for loading styles globally would for example be to load them in the [App.vue](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/src/App.vue) file, or through a css loader configured in vite.

The frontend currently loads ~900KB just stylesheets on the settings page, a lot of which is just duplicated code.

### How to reproduce

Look at any component through your browser's dev-tools and you'll notice, there's the following style defined over and over: 

```css
* {
    -webkit-user-drag: none;
    -khtml

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2023.6.0b3

### The problem

Homeassistant relies on a combination of the attributes `media_duration`, `media_position` and `media_position_updated_at` to calculate a player's current progress without spamming the DB with new states every second.

MAss supplies the `media_position_updated_at` time as a UNIX timestamp in _seconds_, which leads to a completely unrealistic progress because HAss will use that attribute to create a `new Date()` (see [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/blob/dev/src/data/media-player.ts#L217C3-L220)), and TypeScript expects a numerical parameter for the `Date` constructor to be a timestamp in _milliseconds_. 

Other integrations like the Google Cast integration store the `media_position_updated_at` value as a DateTime Object in ISO format, which is much less likely to get parsed wrongly, I'd suggest that MAss does the same.

This problem causes Media Player Lovelace cards to be stuck at 100% progress while the player is playing.
While the player is paused, the `media_position_updated_at` argument is ignored and the HAss frontend calculated the progress directly from duration and position, w

This is a feature request to add the HEOS platform as a Player Provider.

The [Home Assistant HEOS integration](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/heos) itself is using following library: pyheos ([Github](https://github.com/andrewsayre/pyheos) & [PyPi](https://pypi.org/project/pyheos/)). Last update is from August 2022 on Github but November 2020 on PyPi. 

There's other repo's as well, heospy for example ([Github](https://pypi.org/project/heospy/) & [PyPi](https://pypi.org/project/heospy/)). Both are last updated in 2022. Seems like it has a different approach though as it look more like a wrapper to use the CLI commands to control a HEOS device. So perhaps not usable.

In general not too many libraries to be honest (or at least no Python libraries). Hope it's possible to add to MA though, because it's one of the few platforms that also supports HiRes audio up to 24bits 192kHz.

Thanks in advance!

From a post by @postlund in https://github.com/music-assistant/hass-music-assistant/discussions/438#discussioncomment-3031159_
I understand that there is currently a filter in place, which just hides non-Apple devices:

> The filter only applies to discovery though, so it should be possible to add a device manually via IP (assuming the device support AirPlay v1). The streaming support is a bit unstable as it's very early in the development process. Especially when streaming from a remote source, e.g. via https (which is used by TTS) it will likely fail in a lot of cases. There's a very little buffer and pyatv does not handle buffer underruns very good.

I found no reference how such devices could be added manually in HASS.

**Request**
Make a slider so you can set the minimum and max absolute levels for announcements. If the current volume of the player is less than the minimum level, the announcement will be louder than the current music, because it will be at minimum level.

**Description**
Currently you can only set a relative volume level for announcements. This does not work in all cases, for example when we play some background music on our Google Audio and an announcement is being made you can barely hear it because it only increases the volume for say 20%. Just increasing this relative volume will also not always work because sometimes this is just too loud. I want my announcements always to be on say level 40% when the current volume level is less than 40%. So even if we play music on say 20% volume the announcement is still made on 40% volume level. But when we are having a party and the volume of the music is 60% the announcement should also be on 60% because there might be a lot of background noise. But there should be an option to limit this also.

posts.excerpt:
ESPHome's Media Player currently seems to support only MP3 streams. MP3 is a lossy format, sound quality is degraded.
Music Assistant integration by default renders the audio streams in FLAC, which is a lossless format.
Would be nice to enable support in ESPHome for other codecs too:
- lossless FLAC
- uncompressed PCM up to 48k stereo
- open source OPUS (which is lossy, but way better than MP3)
- AAC (also lossy, but better than MP3 and OPUS)

Since only MP3 is supported, one needs to use other firmware than ESPHome, like squeezelite. The goal would be not to have to rely on third party stuff, but remain in the Home Assistant + ESPHome ecosystem.

Adding more codecs of course needs PSRAM for ESP32 (like WROVER module), which is not a problem as plenty of such modules are available. This just needs to be pointed out properly in the documentation.

Also requested in ESPHome FR repo: https://github.com/esphome/feature-requests/issues/1848

posts.excerpt:
Music Assistant has full support of the "Google Cast" platform and it is in fact one of the preferred solutions to use Music Assistant. The cast platform is used on the Google line-up of speakers such as the Google (Nest) Home and Hub but also a very wide range of other manufacturers adopted the Cast platform such as JBL, Harman Kardon and Sony. So in theory you can have a group of speakers from different brands playing the same music in perfect sync.

**General notes**

- Home Assistant documentation for the cast integration: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cast/
- Music Assistant streams audio to the speaker(s) using a local streaming service hosted on TCP port 8095 by default. make sure this port is reachable from your cast speakers on the local network. The IP sent to the speaker is resolved from the "internal URL" field within the Home Assistant configuration. 

**Features:**

- Supports all speakers supported by the cast integration form Home Assistant
- Supports Google cast groups, they will be listed as speaker group in the Music Assistant interface
- Due to the fact that the cast platform has no "power" support, Music Assistant will automatically use mute as pow

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2022.8.0

### The problem

Devices are connecting to mass using an autogenerated url and a static port. This doesn't make much room for advanced setups where you have home-assistant running behind a reverse-proxy, inside kubernetes or similar, making it hard and even impossible on some setups to get mass running.

### How to reproduce

Try to setup mass where the autodetected url is not the one the cast devices can reach mass on.

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Additional information

I run home-assistant inside kubernetes behind a reverse proxy. I've exposed the mass endpoint using kubernetes ingress.
Changing https://github.com/music-assistant/music-assistant-lib/blob/b02a58d89ff448604127f8db2a6f1af7dc785aac/music_assistant/controllers/streams.py#L59 to `https://mass.mydomain.com` instead of the default `f"http://{self._ip}:{self._port}"` made my setup work.

A good way to handle advanced setups is therefor to make this field configurable..

posts.excerpt:
Many Spotify users (including me) have configured and actively are using so-called music scrobbling. Scrobbling is recording the basic details about the song you just listen to like its title, artist or the name of the record and of course the timestamp. The most popular is last.fm but there are more like Libre.fm, ( based on gnu.fm open source) or ListenBrainz. 

Using this kind of service we can generate our database with statistics about the most frequently listened songs, records, and artists accessible for each day, month or any year in the past. This gives us unlimited possibilities to create our own dynamic playlists on Spotify or on other music providers (using tools like soundiiz.com). 

I can imagine having scrobbling stats kept (either locally and merged with my past activity or in the last.fm sent from HA in one batch) and can ask local AI to create and play my favourite songs **in the order which I want or shuffled exactly as I want** (say shuffling all songs from only one artist or only one mood or for example my favourite songs in May 2009). Alternatively the same could be achievable by sorting data in the Music Assistant UI, if we could create that kind of database

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2022.6.6

### The problem

I have a music library mounted from my NAS via SMB to `/media/music`. I have "filesystem provider" enabled for this path in the music assistant integration configuration. The integration successfully imported 38 albums from the library, but then encountered a `FileNotFoundError` on one of the files, which stopped the entire import. When I fixed the problem with the filename, the rest of the import proceeded okay. I expect you want the `filesystem` provider to be more resilient than this.

### How to reproduce

Place a file named "test∕file.flac" (note the unicode division slash character) in a smb mountpoint that is scanned by the filesystem provider. Wait for it to do a scan and you should see the crash error in the HA core log. This might also be reproducible simply by placing a file with this name, or possibly any unicode character, in a regular local directory read by the filesystem provider.

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2022.6.4

### The problem

running the shell_command to mount my Nas drive (testing that functionality) works just fine. But.... my Nas is turned down to sleepmode each night for power savings.

I didnt realize that could inhibit the Music Assistant install using that Mount until now.

this morning I see below errors in the logs, which of course relate to that. To my surprise the actual files in the mount are still visible, via the Media/Local files browser, and, more surprisingly after reading that error in the log, to Music Assistant!

I would have expected Music Assistant, sensing the drive had disappeared, to update the DB and delete those files in a whim. It didnt.

Only posting it here as a FYI, and maybe for others to test this functionality.

There's no use in automating some kind of re-mount in the morning, because this is a) a temporary configuration, and b) it wont prevent MA from wiping during the Sleep time.

Yet is is something to consider going forward, in designing the MA's core support for NAS drives, and not delete the DB during sleep time

### How to reproduce

mount a nas drive with the known shell command

posts.excerpt:
Let's say you have a party and you want your guests to have control over the music. Just like an old-school jukebox.
Globally my idea is as follows:

- Create some option/button to enable "guest/party mode" on a Queue.
- Have some easy way for guests to control the queue, for example a separate web URL and/or simple app.
- It must be plain simple, for example have a QR code or other share code to share the guest login with your guests
- Once the party is over you withdraw the party mode.
- Guests can add songs to the queue
- You (as host) select the main playlist and from which music the guests may pick (default to all music from all providers)
- You (as host) select the add mode in which way tracks are added to the queue. For example FIFO which will place each guest request after the current playing track (but in order of arrival) or random which will insert the tracks somewhere within the queue or "dj mode" where the track is intelligently inserted in the queue based on surrounding music and number of requests
- Guests are not able to do volume control on the queue ?
- Guests are not able to pause/play the music ?

posts.excerpt:
The library items are retrieved by the frontend when you open the panel all-at-once.
So all Artists are loaded in one batch, All Albums etc.

For people with larger collections this comes with a performance penalty:

1) There's a real large chunk of data being moved from db --> MA --> HA --> websocket --> frontend
2) It takes a while before the frontend is useable, you have to wait until the data is precached into the "store" of the frontend.
3) The HA executor is busy creating large chunks of data, I believe @bdraco has recently seen a profiler report showing this.

Solution here would be to move the item listings around as smaller chunks.
Like prefetch the first 250 items and request more if you scroll around the listings (or slowly prefetch them if you are navigating)

Not a very large job to adjust but needs to be done properly. Too much to make it into the 2022.6 release tomorrow.
This task is a reminder.

There are several issues reported directly or more indirect belonging to this issue.
- websocket can't keep up error by @erkr 
- memory consumption by @K3str3l
- load times by @Mariusthvdb
posts.title: Retrieve library listings in smaller chunks

posts.excerpt:
Let's say you have a party and you want your guests to have control over the music. Just like an old-school jukebox.
Globally my idea is as follows:

- Create some option/button to enable "guest/party mode" on a Queue.
- Have some easy way for guests to control the queue, for example a separate web URL and/or simple app.
- It must be plain simple, for example have a QR code or other share code to share the guest login with your guests
- Once the party is over you withdraw the party mode.
- Guests can add songs to the queue
- You (as host) select the main playlist and from which music the guests may pick (default to all music from all providers)
- You (as host) select the add mode in which way tracks are added to the queue. For example FIFO which will place each guest request after the current playing track (but in order of arrival) or random which will insert the tracks somewhere within the queue or "dj mode" where the track is intelligently inserted in the queue based on surrounding music and number of requests
- Guests are not able to do volume control on the queue ?
- Guests are not able to pause/play the music ?

posts.excerpt:
Since the streams on TuneIn are actually created by the radio station operators themselves, and these are in many cases Shoutcast or Icecast streams, containing embedded ICY metadata in the structure of `Artist - Title` or just `Show name`, this could be extracted from the stream if found in it.

A hacky way to extract data can be seen [here](https://github.com/nagyrobi/home-assistant-custom-components-linkplay/blob/7ff9153327296274d4384cb7b31c178634e0a1ca/custom_components/linkplay/media_player.py#L1818). This is far from optimal because it doesn't actually play the stream it just connects to the server and grabs the headers periodically. The correct way would be (and can be done with MA) to get this info from the original stream before transcoding, and that could update metadata in real time.

This is just textual information, and ICY metadata usually don't contain coverart links. So for radio stations one could keep the radio station logo as cover art.

The audio stream is sent as raw audio stream (optionally encoded to flac or other codec) to a player.
This means that players with a small display do not show any metadata whats playing.

One of the solutions could be to implement ICY metadata but I'm not so sure if players do still request/support that.
I have checked a few players in my house (e.g. Chromecast) and None of them actually sent the ICY-Meta header but maybe I'm overlooking something.

If enough interest I can add this in but for now I consider this low prio.

Anyone interested in (re)acting to the metadata of MA [can subscribe to the HA eventbus `mass_event`](https://github.com/music-assistant/hass-music-assistant/pull/125)
